## Load libraries

```{r}
#| label: load-libraries
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(broom)
```


## Load data

```{r}
#| label: task-1

raw_dir <- here("data", "_raw")
data_file <- "gravier.RData"
data_loc <- "https://github.com/ramhiser/datamicroarray/raw/master/data/"

if( !dir.exists(raw_dir) ){
  dir.create(path = raw_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}
if( !file.exists(here(raw_dir, data_file)) ){
  download.file(
    url = str_c(data_loc, data_file),
    destfile = here(raw_dir, data_file),
    mode = "wb")
}
load(file = here(raw_dir, data_file))
```


Q2: It's not tidy data, it's a list without named columns and proper formatting

## Clean data

```{r}
#| label: task-2

gravier_clean <- gravier |>
  bind_cols() |>
  as_tibble()
```

Q3: Now, it's more tidy: 
- Each column is a distinct variable (gene expression)
- Each row is an observation
- Each cell has an experimental value
BUT the good/poor status of the patients is mixed with the other gene columns, is this tidy?

Q5: bind_cols bind data_frames by column. So if some data frames are not using the same format, or are observations of different data sets, or just are sorted in a different way, you can easily mix some observations

### Write clean data to disk

```{r}
#| label: task-3

clean_dir <- "data"
clean_file <- "02_gravier_clean.tsv.gz"

if( !dir.exists(here(clean_dir)) ){
  dir.create(path = here(clean_dir), recursive = TRUE)
}

write_tsv(x = gravier_clean,
          file = here(clean_dir, clean_file))
```


## Augment data

```{r}
#| label: task-4

gravier_clean_aug <- gravier_clean |>
  mutate(y = case_when(y == "poor" ~ 1,
                       y == "good" ~ 0)) |> 
  relocate(early_metastasis = y)
```

```{r}
#| label: task-5

clean_aug_file <- "03_gravier_clean_aug.tsv.gz"

write_tsv(x = gravier_clean_aug,
          file = here(clean_dir, clean_aug_file))
```

## Analysis

```{r}
#| label: task-7

my_first_model <- lm(formula = g1E11 ~ early_metastasis, data = gravier_clean_aug)
my_first_model
```

```{r}
#| label: task-8

gravier_clean_aug |>
  group_by(early_metastasis) |>
  summarize(mean(g1E11))
```

Q9: We have: Intercept = mean for (early_meastasis=0) and slope = difference between the means

Q10: My gene is down_regulated from early_metastasis=1

```{r}
#| label: question-10

my_first_model |> summary()
```

The p_value is around 0.11, so there's no statistical evidence that there is an association between g1E11 expression and early metastasis

Q12: gravier_clean_aug is a wide dataset: one row contains all the gene expressions for one patient

```{r}
#| label: task-9

gravier_clean_aug_long <- gravier_clean_aug |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -early_metastasis,
               names_to = "gene",
               values_to = "log2_expr_level")
```

```{r}
#| label: task-10

gravier_clean_aug_long_nested <- gravier_clean_aug_long |>
  group_by(gene) |>
  nest() 

gravier_clean_aug_long_nested
```


```{r}
#| label: seed

set.seed(42) # In case I do sampling later and want to have a reproducible workflow
```

```{r}
#| label: task-12

gravier_clean_aug_long_nested <- gravier_clean_aug_long_nested |>
  group_by(gene) |>
  mutate(model_object = map(.x = data,
                   .f = ~lm(formula = log2_expr_level ~ early_metastasis,
                            data = .x)))
```

```{r}
#| label: test-task-12

gravier_clean_aug_long_nested |>
  filter(gene == "g1E11") |> 
  pull(model_object)
```


```{r}
#| label: tidying models

gravier_clean_aug_long_nested |>
  
  filter(gene == "g1E11") |> 
  
  # Pull() on tibbles: This pulls out the model_object variable.
  #   Note! This is a list, because we nested!
  pull(model_object) |> 
  
  # Pluck() on lists: From the list we got from the last step,
  #   we "pluck" the first element
  pluck(1) |>
  
  # The result of pluck, is a model object,
  #   upon which we can call the tidy function
  tidy(conf.int = TRUE,
       conf.level = 0.95)
```

```{r}
#| label: task-13

gravier_clean_aug_long_nested <- gravier_clean_aug_long_nested |>
  group_by(gene) |>
  mutate(model_object_tidy =  map(.x = model_object,
                                  .f = ~tidy(x = .x,
                                             conf.int = TRUE,
                                             conf.level = 0.95)))
```

## Data wrangling

```{r}
#| label: task-14

gravier_estimates <- gravier_clean_aug_long_nested |>
  unnest(model_object_tidy)
```

```{r}
#| label: task-15

gravier_estimates <- gravier_estimates |>
  filter(term == "early_metastasis") |>
  select("gene", "p.value", "estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high") |>
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
#| label: task-16

gravier_estimates <- gravier_estimates |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(q.value = p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni"), # This is the default method
         is_significant = if_else(q.value > 0.05, "no", "yes"))
```


```{r}
#| label: task-17

gravier_estimates_significant <- gravier_estimates |>
  filter(is_significant == "yes") |>
  mutate(gene = fct_reorder(gene, estimate))

ggplot(data = gravier_estimates_significant,
       mapping = aes(x = estimate,
                     xmin = conf.low,
                     xmax = conf.high,
                     y = gene)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
  geom_errorbarh() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Estimates (95% Cls)",
       title = "Genes Associated with Early Metastasis in Small Node-Negative Breast Carcinoma") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| label: task-18

library(ggrepel)

gravier_estimates <- gravier_estimates |>
  mutate(significant_gene = if_else(is_significant == "yes", gene, ""))

ggplot(data = gravier_estimates,
       mapping = aes(x = estimate,,
                     y = - log10(p.value),
                     label = significant_gene,
                     color = is_significant)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_text_repel() +
  labs(x = "Estimates (95% Cls)",
       y = "-log10(p)",
       title = "Genes Associated with Early Metastasis in Small Node-Negative Breast Carcinoma",
       subtitle = "Genes highlited in turquoise were significant after multiple testing correction") +
  theme_minimal()
```
